evidence: X-ray diffraction and infrared spectroscopy measurements are conducted in order to assess the crystallographic structure and chemical purity of lanthanum oxide films grown by atomic layer deposition on Si substrates. Structural information in terms of identifying crystallographic phases and estimating their relative amount in the as-grown and annealed La2O3 films was obtained through grazing incidence X-ray diffraction while film thickness was evaluated with the aid of specular X-ray reflectivity. The X-ray diffractometer was equipped with a sealed Cu X-ray tube, parabolic multilayer monochromator to select K radiation, and a system of crossed slits defining the beam size. The presence of organic ligand residuals or contaminant species in the as-grown and annealed La2O3 films was probed through transmission mode Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy in the 500–4000 cm−1 range.
